## Why This Is Asked

This task tests design of an on-device data pipeline that handles multiple sensors, preserves privacy, and remains resilient across app lifecycle while considering power constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Modular data pipeline with explicit stages and clear data flow
- Swift concurrency: actors for thread safety and isolation
- HealthKit, CoreMotion, and BLE integration with normalization
- On-device privacy: hashing identifiers (SHA-256)
- Crash-safe durable queue (SQLite) with replay on launch
- Backpressure and adaptive sampling for power efficiency
- SwiftUI dashboard for live metrics

## Code Example

```swift

  func process(_ input: DataPoint) async -> DataPoint?
}
actor IngestStage: Stage { /* collects HealthKit/CoreMotion/BLE data */ }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test backpressure under low-power mode and offline scenarios?
- How would you evolve the persisted schema without losing older data?

## Why This Is Asked
Assessing ability to design privacy-preserving data pipelines, on-device processing, and robust offline syncing. This probes DP reasoning, data modeling, and test strategy under real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Local differential privacy and privacy budgets
- On-device data transformation and storage (SQLite)
- Batched network uploads with fault tolerance
- Crash-safe persistence and resume semantics
- SwiftUI UI for DP-protected metrics

## Code Example
```swift
// Pseudo: DP noise helper
func dpNoise(value: Double, epsilon: Double) -> Double {
    // Laplace mechanism placeholder
    let scale = 1.0 / epsilon
    return value + Laplace.sample(scale: scale)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test DP calibration without exposing real user data?
- How would you handle drift in epsilon budget over long deployments?

Tests end-to-end iOS data flow: data modeling in Core Data, offline-first persistence, de-duplication and backpressure, deterministic replay for analytics, crash-resume handling, and a concrete test plan—critical for senior roles at Google and Amazon.

Key Concepts

- Offline-first pipeline with per-device streams
- Core Data schema design and migrations
- De-duplication by composite key and high-rate buffering
- Time-based aggregates (1s/1m) and deterministic replay
- Lightweight, idempotent sync protocol and crash resilience
- Comprehensive test strategy (unit, integration, performance)

Code Example

```swift
// Core Data NSManagedObject subclasses example
class Device: NSManagedObject { @NSManaged var id: String; @NSManaged var name: String }
class Session: NSManagedObject { @NSManaged var id: String; @NSManaged var startedAt: Date }
class Event: NSManagedObject { @NSManaged var deviceID: String; @NSManaged var timestamp: Date; @NSManaged var type: String; @NSManaged var payload: Data; @NSManaged var session: Session? }
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you design migrations for zero-downtime schema changes?
- How would you validate deterministic replay under intermittent connectivity and data loss?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes cross-device AR synchronization, offline resilience, and conflict resolution—skills valuable for real-world AR apps at scale.

## Key Concepts

- ARKit anchors, world tracking, anchor fusion
- CloudKit/REST sync, version vectors, CRDT-like merges
- Offline-first design, conflict resolution UX
- Testing: drift, race conditions, reconciliation

## Code Example

```swift
struct AnchorRecord: Codable {
  let id: String
  var posX: Float; var posY: Float; var posZ: Float
  var rotX: Float; var rotY: Float; var rotZ: Float; var rotW: Float
  var version: Int
}
func merge(remote: AnchorRecord, local: inout AnchorRecord) {
  if remote.version > local.version {
    local = remote
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you detect and resolve anchor drift during long AR sessions?
- What backend schema supports millions of anchors across devices?
